topic: False news travels faster than the truth
subject: social

facts.claim: Robots accelerated the spread of true and false news at the same rate.
facts.quote: Contrary to conventional wisdom, robots accelerated the spread of true and false news at the same rate, implying that false news spreads more than the truth because humans, not robots, are more likely to spread it.

facts.claim: Participants were better at rating false news as false than at rating true news as true.
facts.quote: We found that people rated true news as more accurate than false news (Cohen’s d = 1.12 [1.01, 1.22]) and were better at rating false news as false than at rating true news as true (Cohen’s d = 0.32 [0.24, 0.39]).

facts.claim: False news was more novel than true news.
facts.quote: We found that false news was more novel than true news, which suggests that people were more likely to share novel information.

facts.claim: User interactions with false content rose steadily on both Facebook and Twitter through the end of 2016, but have since fallen sharply on Facebook while continuing to rise on Twitter.
facts.quote: User interactions with false content rose steadily on both Facebook and Twitter through the end of 2016. Since then, however, interactions with false content have fallen sharply on Facebook while continuing to rise on Twitter

facts.claim: Falsehood diffused significantly farther, faster, deeper, and more broadly than the truth in all categories of information.
facts.quote: Falsehood diffused significantly farther, faster, deeper, and more broadly than the truth in all categories of information

facts.claim: Participants who paused to explain why a headline was true or false indicated that they were less likely to share false information compared to control participants.
facts.quote: In an online experiment, participants who paused to explain why a headline was true or false indicated that they were less likely to share false information compared to control participants.

research.angle: False news spreads faster and further than truth because humans are more likely to share novel information that inspires fear, disgust, and surprise.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that false news spreads more effectively than truth due to human behavior and novelty, though people are generally capable of discerning falsehoods.
research.caveat: While false news spreads more broadly, its relative magnitude on Facebook has declined since 2016 while continuing to rise on Twitter.
